title: Auto Loans: Days Past Due, Delinquency and Charge-Off
content:
An Auto Loans account's standing is driven by one counter, its days past due. This policy defines the counter and the status changes it produces.

## The counter

Days past due are the calendar days that have elapsed since the due date of the earliest installment still unsatisfied. The counter goes back to zero when every installment that was past due has been satisfied.

## Status changes

| Days past due | Status consequence |
|---|---|
| Reaches the product's delinquency threshold | the loan becomes delinquent |
| Returns to zero on a delinquent loan | the loan becomes active again |
| Reaches the product's charge-off threshold | the whole unpaid principal is written off and the debt passes to recovery |

This policy does not govern repossession, settlements, hardship modifications or payment plans on loans that have fallen behind.

## Reading the counter (hypothetical dates)

If the earliest unsatisfied installment fell due on 15 February 2031, the loan shows 14 days past due on 1 March 2031. A payment on that day which satisfies that installment, with no other installment past due, brings the counter back to zero; if a second installment were also past due, the counter would then be measured from that second installment's due date.
